articles.title: Avengers: Doomsday has brought with it more ‘Marvel homework’ than ever. That’s just as it should be
articles.summary: Working out where returning hero Steve Rogers has been is only one of the multiversal puzzles fans must now get their heads around – which is catnip for the connoisseurs.
body: The cinema release of Avengers: Doomsday is now roughly three weeks away and, judging by the final trailer, we’re living in the one timeline where every loose end Marvel has left dangling for years is now worth tugging on. Even the ones we thought the studio had tied up rather nicely. Ever since it became apparent that Chris Evans’ Steve Rogers would be returning in the new film, along with next year’s sequel Avengers: Secret Wars, fans have been asking themselves: where exactly has he been all this time? Now, thanks to the latest footage, we’re beginning to get an idea, and we might also be starting to pick up clues as to why Doctor Doom would take an interest in his new postcode.

One of the most startling aspects of the new trailer is the arrival of the Fantastic Four, led by Pedro Pascal’s Reed Richards, on Rogers’ front lawn. We’ve known since the finale of Avengers: Endgame that Steve used Tony Stark’s newly discovered time-travelling tech to go back to the 1940s and live out his life with Peggy Carter during the events of that film – but until recently it seemed most likely that happened in good old Earth-616, the main Marvel Cinematic Universe continuity.

articles.title: Get me a 747 and deploy the oxygen masks! The British pilot behind Hollywood’s greatest inflight scenes
articles.summary: An emergency landing for Bridesmaids, a humiliation for Ben Stiller in Focker-in-Law, a giant toilet for Britney Spears in the Toxic video … Richard Chan, No 1 provider of airplane cabin sets, recalls his finest work.
body: With Thanksgiving having just kicked off holiday season in the US, millions of people are boarding flights, many more concerned than ever about how chaotic that might be. Aside from the shock of the recent FAA shutdown, not a day seems to go by without a viral video of someone behaving badly or being removed from an airplane: Saturday Night Live even did a sketch about the introduction of a “new airline class”, with a whole section of a plane reserved for “crazy people”.

In the big Thanksgiving movie Focker-In-Law, Ben Stiller has a lengthy and awkward encounter with a flight attendant who is summoned by a passenger called Olivia, played by Ariana Grande. On arrival, he learns that Olivia is his potential daughter-in-law and, of course, that means more trouble with his ex-CIA father-in-law Jack, played by Robert De Niro.

articles.title: Spain Nears New India Co-Production Pact as It Wraps Country of Honor Run at IFFI Goa, WAVES Film Bazaar
articles.summary: Spain and India have moved closer to a fresh film and audiovisual co-production treaty as Spain wrapped its run as Country of Honor at the 57th International Film Festival of India (IFFI) in Goa and its market, WAVES Film Bazaar. On Nov.
body: Spain Film Commission, the non-profit umbrella group for Spain’s film commissions and film offices, organized the Spanish program in Goa alongside ICAA, which sits under the Ministry of Culture. ICEX–Invest in Spain and Casa de la India provided support. Funding came from the Ministry of Culture and from the Ministry for Digital Transformation and Public Administration, via its Secretary of State for Digitalization and Artificial Intelligence (SEDIA), under the Spain Audiovisual Hub Plan.

“Our participation in IFFI Goa is part of a collaboration strategy that we have been developing with the Indian audiovisual industry for several years. Spain’s recognition as Country of Honor at this edition represents an important milestone, reflecting this collective effort and our close cooperation with ICAA and the other institutions involved. At Spain Film Commission, we will continue to promote these partnerships to create new opportunities for co-production, investment and filming across Spain’s territories,” said Juan Manuel Guimeráns, president of Spain Film Commission.

articles.title: South African President Cyril Ramaphosa Gives Speech at Canal+ Academy Training Program Launch: ‘You Are Living My Dream’
articles.summary: The new pan-African initiative will expand training and professional development opportunities for local aspiring professionals in the creative industries. The momentous event — which saw South Africa’s leader, Canal+ CEO Maxime Saada
body: Ramaphosa praised Canal+’s investment in MultiChoice and its decision to make the country an African media market hub, while also lauding the academy as a way to build Africa’s film and TV industry and expand opportunities for young people.

“Today, we are celebrating a significant moment in the country’s broadcasting and creative industries,” Ramaphosa said, adding: “I am very envious, because in my private life I’ve often said that one day I’d like to produce a movie.”
He quipped, “What I’m doing currently, it’s OK. But now, you are living my dream.”

South Africa is becoming the first market to introduce the Canal + Academy model. The program, which incorporates the existing MultiChoice Talent Factory, aims to reach between 800 and 1,000 beneficiaries during its first 12 months.

articles.title: Luc Besson Jokes That He Could Make the Next ‘Terminator,’ but Only if the Terminator ‘Sat Down and Said He Missed His Mom’
articles.summary: Luc Besson rejects the idea that he reinvented action cinema. He simply used to have the freedom to experiment. “When you don’t have a lot of experience, you have all this freedom. You aren’t controlled by big studios and 50 people telling you why you can’t do something because it costs too much.
body: “When Modigliani wanted to paint women with long necks and black eyes, that’s what he did. We need to take this freedom back because we are simply killing art. We’re turning it into something that can be sold, like yogurt or socks. There are four crucial things in the lives of men and women: Water, air, love and art. Without them, we’re dead.”
He added, “Now, we have replaced everything with money. And it’s going to kill us all.”

Besson was speaking at Torino Film Festival, where he received the Stella delle Mole award for lifetime achievement. Earlier that day, he deadpanned, “I saw the list of all the people who have received it, and I didn’t understand why I hadn’t received it too. I’m not used to receiving awards in my own country, so I’m happy to receive one abroad.”
Celebrated for “The Big Blue,” “Léon: The Professional,” “ The Fifth Element ” and “Lucy,” Besson was honest about his preferences.
points: Luc Besson rejects the idea that he reinvented action cinema.
He simply used to have the freedom to experiment.
“When you don’t have a lot of experience, you have all this freedom.
You aren’t controlled by big studios and 50 people telling you why you can’t do something because it costs too much.

articles.title: ‘Dangal’ Casting Director Mukesh Chhabra Recalls Auditioning Nearly 14,000 Girls, Shares Self-Tape Tips at IFFI Masterclass
articles.summary: Mukesh Chhabra, the casting director behind “Dangal” and Shah Rukh Khan’s upcoming “King,” took aspiring actors and filmmakers behind the scenes of the casting process at a masterclass at the 57th International Film Festival of India (IFFI) in Goa.
body: Introducing Chhabra, festival director Ashutosh Gowariker, whose “Lagaan” was nominated for the foreign-language film Oscar, said, “What I like about Mukesh is his eye for character and he will go to any length to find the actors who fit in.”

Chhabra, whose casting credits include “Dhurandhar,” Aamir Khan’s “Dangal,” Anurag Kashyap’s “Gangs of Wasseypur,” Nitesh Tiwari’s “Ramayana” and “King,” due Dec. 24, described the casting director’s role as a bridge between actors and directors. His work begins with understanding a script and the director’s vision, then determining whether a character calls for an established face or someone new.

“There is so much talent in our country,” he said. “I send my team all over the country to scout for talent. You have to go to the roots. Our country has so many cultural arts and sub-cultures where so much raw talent is displayed.” Directors, he added, hire him for “my opinion, my ideas, not for my data.”

The scale of the search can be considerable. For “Dangal,” he recalled auditioning nearly 14,000 girls over almost two years. For “Gangs of Wasseypur,” he cast 384 people. That film, he said, “changed my life.”

articles.title: ‘Everybody tells me how I can keep working. My answer begins with ‘F’ and ends with ‘off’: Mike Leigh on 55 years of films – and why he’s just made his last
articles.summary: The acclaimed director has announced his latest film Tender Loving Care will be his last. He talks about coming to terms with a life-changing condition and how he would have loved to have made a big budget modern-day movie.
body: Mike Leigh and his partner, the actor Marion Bailey, were knocking around at home last Christmas, looking for a good film to watch and constantly coming up short. Finally, Leigh had a brilliant idea. Why not put on Topsy-Turvy, his 1999 costume romp about the making of The Mikado? Problem solved, perfect choice. “It’s not like a habit,” he says hurriedly. “I don’t sit there watching my films every night like Gloria Swanson in Sunset Boulevard. It’s just that Topsy-Turvy happens to be a very enjoyable watch.”

The way Leigh sees it, his films are like children. They’ve outgrown him, moved on, but it’s nice to check the family ties are still strong. Some are sunny (Life is Sweet; Happy-Go-Lucky) and some are dour (Naked; Hard Truths), but they all share the same DNA, the same real-world interests and tragicomic mindset. He can’t choose between them; he’ll defend each one to the death. Then he pauses and says, “But I’ve got a soft spot for Meantime.”

He talks about coming to terms with a life-changing condition and how he would have loved to have made a big budget modern-day movie.

articles.title: Five Gladiators will not return for new BBC series
articles.summary: The programme is set to feature a host of new faces when it returns to screens next year.
body: Five Gladiators stars will not be returning to the BBC television show for its upcoming series, it is understood.
Athena, Comet, Bionic, Phantom and Cyclone will not be featured when the show returns in 2027.
A spokesperson for the production said the departing cast members "remain part of the wider Gladiators family" and are taking part in the ongoing arena tour, which comes to an end in December.
Gladiators relaunched on the BBC in 2024, having originally been aired on ITV from 1992 until 2000, and then on Sky between 2008 and 2009.

articles.title: Justin Timberlake Rolls Back the Years on Silly, Sexy and Sincere Appearance on ‘Tonight Show’
articles.summary: The singer performed a medley of his hits, took part in some dumb sketches and bared his soul about why he agreed to take part in an upcoming Apple TV docuseries.
body: A game Justin Timberlake gave a welcome reminder of his varied talents on The Tonight Show on Thursday night, variously dressing up as a “sexy” turkey, doing a spirited Scottish accent and of course dancing and singing like only he can.

With the Roots backing them up, Fallon opened the show with Timberlake for a song and dance number, with the duo going through The History of Party Songs. In a segment that is catnip for 90s kids, the tracks covered included Soul II Soul’s “Back to Life (However Do You Want Me),” Ini Kamoze’s “Here Comes the Hotstepper,” Mark Morrison’s “Return of the Mack,” Montell Jordan’s “This Is How We Do It,” Spice Girls “Wannabe,” Bell Biv DeVoe’s “Poison,” Timberlake’s own “Rock Your Body” and more.
On the infamous lyrics to “SexyBack”, Timberlake added, “That song does not make any sense. I’ve said this. It makes zero sense. But, it’s why it makes sense.”

articles.title: You Can See Everything overtly riffs on Vertigo. But how big is its debt to Kiarostami’s Close-Up?
articles.summary: The Iranian film-maker’s 1990 tale of impersonation and deception happens to be a favourite movie of the Elizabeth Holmes docufiction’s co-director Lance Oppenheim • NB: This article contains spoilers.
body: You’re probably sick of hearing how You Can See Everything, about the disgraced Theranos founder Elizabeth Holmes, is the buzziest, coolest, 100% freshest film of the year, but coming out of the screening last week, I couldn’t help but wonder whether Nathan Fielder and Lance Oppenheim had been watching a lot of 90s Iranian cinema. And one film in particular: Close-Up, by Abbas Kiarostami.

If it feels as if You Can See Everything blends truth, lies, fiction and documentary in mind-bending new ways until you’re no longer sure what the hell you’re watching, then Kiarostami, who died in 2016, practically invented this mode 36 years ago. The context could not be more different – analogue 90s Tehran rather than tech-drunk 2020s California – but the themes are the same: Close-Up is a strange story of impersonation, deception and performance, made even stranger by the film-maker’s deliberate meddling.

articles.title: Huw Edwards gives first interviews since child abuse image conviction
articles.summary: Minister Anna Turley said she was "deeply uncomfortable" with the interviews, while Channel 4 has insisted it "holds Edwards to account".
body: Disgraced former BBC News presenter Huw Edwards has given his first interviews since being convicted in 2024 for making indecent images of children.
Edwards is seen saying he believes "silence is toxic" in a clip of a podcast released by the Observer newspaper, and he has also been interviewed for a Channel 4 documentary.
Government minister Anna Turley told LBC, external she was "deeply uncomfortable" with the interviews, while shadow culture secretary Rebecca Paul said: "This man shouldn't get a minute of airtime".

Channel 4 has defended the documentary. A spokesperson told the BBC that a "highly experienced director" holds Edwards to account with "no questions off limits, revealing his account of what led to his offending and very public downfall".
